transcript.content: Hello, thanks for coming in today. What brings you in?

Well, they say I’m here because of what I've been doing at the house. I used our savings on a bunch of wood, lights, and display stuff. I just kept at it, you know, pushing the work long after dark to get it set up. They were upset about the money and the late nights, but... I just felt like if I stopped, the whole house, the whole block really, would lose its chance. So I had to keep going.
During this period, did you need less sleep than usual while still feeling rested?

I'm not really sure about that. I mean, I know I was staying up real late working on the lights and the wood and everything, but... I don't know if I felt rested, exactly. I didn't really pay attention to it. I just slept whenever I finally stopped working.
Before these changes began, had you used any recreational drugs or taken medications differently than prescribed?

No, I don't... I don't mess with any of that. No drugs. And as for my regular pills, I just take them the way the doctor told me to. I didn't take anything extra or different before all this started, if that's what you mean.
During this period, did you feel unusually euphoric or unusually happy most of the day?

Well, yeah, I'd say so. Most days I feel really charged up... almost joyful, honestly. It's like I'm young again, getting all this work done. But I will say, if my wife or the contractors start questioning me about what I'm doing, I get hot fast. I just lose my temper and start yelling at them.
Do you still believe that your work was necessary to save the whole block, even when other people told you it was not?

Yeah, I do. I know people think I’m all mixed up about this, but... I'm sure this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. I just know it. And it's not just in my head, either. Little things prove it, like... like the trucks slowing down when they drive by, or the neighbors looking over at my yard. They know it too, even if they don't want to admit it out loud.
When you are not feeling unusually energized or irritable, do you still believe that your work is necessary to save the whole neighborhood?

Well, honestly... no. Before I got so charged up with all the remodeling plans, I wasn’t seeing any special meaning in the trucks slowing down or the neighbors looking over at me. I didn't think anything of it back then. Those signs... they really only started making sense once I felt driven to turn the house into my big civic project.
Before this current period, have you ever had another distinct period when you felt unusually energized or irritable and behaved in a markedly different way from your usual self?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I've always liked to keep busy over the years, but I've never had a time where I felt this fired up before. This whole thing, having all this energy and getting so worked up over a project... it's really the first time anything like this has happened to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a distinct period of elevated and irritable mood, markedly increased goal-directed activity, excessive spending, and significant behavioral impairment, accompanied by mood-congruent grandiose and referential delusions. Psychotic beliefs reportedly occur only during the energized mood state, and substance or medication causes were denied. Duration and full manic-episode duration criteria were not established.

confirmed_symptoms: Unusually elevated or joyful mood most days
Markedly increased energy and goal-directed activity focused on an extensive civic art/remodeling project
Persisting with work late into the night and difficulty stopping
Excessive spending of household savings on project materials
Marked irritability and frequent yelling when questioned by others
Grandiose belief that the neighborhood was selected for the patient's major civic art project
Belief that the work was necessary to save the whole neighborhood
Referential interpretation of trucks slowing down and neighbors looking at the property as evidence that others recognized the project's significance
Patient reported that the special meaning attributed to trucks and neighbors began with the energized state and was absent before that period
Patient denied continuing to hold these beliefs when not unusually energized or irritable
Denied recreational drug use before symptom onset
Denied taking prescribed medication differently or taking extra medication

additional_requirements: Psychotic symptoms were explicitly linked to the period of elevated or irritable mood
No prior distinct manic or hypomanic episode was reported
Reduced need for sleep was specifically assessed but not confirmed
